key_insight: Monitored quantum transport crosses between Zeno-suppressed and low-monitoring regimes, with an optimal monitoring period set by the single-particle bandwidth.
engineering_relevance: Monitoring cadence is a practical control parameter for quantum transport, since overly frequent measurements can suppress particle arrival.
method: Study periodically monitored spin chains and quantum circuits.
Measure single- and interacting-particle arrival times on superconducting quantum hardware.
Compare measured distributions with quantum-trajectory theory.
evidence_signal: Measurements in one- and two-dimensional circuits resolve both regimes and closely match theory; interactions reshape distributions while preserving the optimal monitoring point.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify hardware noise, statistical uncertainty, or scalability to larger systems.
paper_title: Arrival-time problem in the quantum information era - observation of a Zeno crossover in monitored arrival-time distributions
